subject.title: [Feature] Control UI should accept gateway token from Authorization header

question: Which reverse-proxy shared-secret bootstrap model should OpenClaw support for Control UI?
rationale: The code can support several shapes, but choosing how proxy headers become Gateway operator credentials affects spoofing protections, origin handling, rate limits, pairing/device semantics, and credential lifetime.

options.title: Use a short-lived browser session
options.body: Validate the proxy header on a same-origin bootstrap endpoint and mint a short-lived browser credential for the WebSocket path.

options.title: Validate headers on WebSocket upgrade
options.body: Accept a purpose-built header such as X-OpenClaw-Token during trusted-proxy WebSocket upgrades after origin, proxy, and rate-limit checks.

options.title: Keep current supported paths
options.body: Decline shared-secret header bootstrap and keep connect.params auth plus identity-bearing Tailscale/trusted-proxy modes as the documented paths.

recommendation.title: Use a short-lived browser session
recommendation.body: Validate the proxy header on a same-origin bootstrap endpoint and mint a short-lived browser credential for the WebSocket path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue and has recent Gateway auth history on the same trust-boundary surface.
